content:
Apple Podcasts is my go-to podcast app, but I've long had issues with its core "Up Next" queue feature. I'm happy to say iOS 27.2 brings a fix.

iOS 27.2 splits Apple Podcasts' "Up Next" queue into two sections: "Latest Episodes" and "Continue Listening"

There's a lot to love about Apple Podcasts. Transcripts and auto-generated chapters are two killer features that make this app my top pick. I'm also a fan of all the recent video-related upgrades.

But for years, Apple Podcasts' core "Up Next" queue has made me want to switch to other apps.

I've already written about why "Up Next" feels broken. In short:

  • It doesn't give you a good view of what shows are available to listen to
  • Some episodes can easily disappear, even if you're partway through them

However, I'm thrilled to say iOS 27.2 brings a long-overdue fix to "Up Next." The solution is to split the feature into two separate sections:

  • Latest Episodes
  • Continue Listening

At the very top of the app is "Latest Episodes," which looks much like the original "Up Next" and functions similarly. The difference is that, as the name suggests, it only shows the newest episode of each show you follow.

"Continue Listening" sits right below, serving as a central hub for all episodes you've started but haven't finished.

Top comments are from Nutmac

Queue management is still messy, and the lack of syncing across devices is baffling.

Together, these two sections solve all my biggest issues with the "Up Next" queue.

I can see at a glance what's new, and I'll never miss episodes again since anything I've started listening to will be in "Continue Listening." I still have a few minor gripes, but these changes alone address my main problems with "Up Next."

If you haven't tried Apple Podcasts in a while, iOS 27.2 is the perfect time to give it another shot.

Do you use Apple or another podcast app? Let us know in the comments.
